cards.front: What is the basic economic problem?
cards.back: Scarcity - unlimited wants but limited resources

cards.front: What are the four factors of production?
cards.back: Land, Labor, Capital, and Entrepreneurship
The value of the next best alternative that is forgone
The quantity of a good that producers are willing to sell at various prices
The quantity of a good that consumers are willing to buy at various prices

cards.front: What is the law of supply?
cards.back: As price increases, quantity supplied increases (ceteris paribus)

cards.front: What is the law of demand?
cards.back: As price increases, quantity demanded decreases (ceteris paribus)
The price at which quantity supplied equals quantity demanded

A sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services
A sustained decrease in the general price level of goods and services
Gross Domestic Product - the total value of goods and services produced in a country
The state of being without a job but actively seeking employment
A market structure with only one seller of a particular good or service
A market structure with many buyers and sellers of identical products
The responsiveness of quantity demanded or supplied to changes in price
A payment from the government to producers to encourage production
A compulsory payment to the government
A tax on imported goods
A limit on the quantity of a good that can be imported
The additional cost of producing one more unit of output
The additional revenue from selling one more unit of output

A maximum price set by the government below the equilibrium price
A minimum price set by the government above the equilibrium price

The difference between what producers receive and what they are willing to accept
The loss of economic efficiency due to market intervention

A good whose demand decreases when income increases

Goods that are used together
